title: Pinworms in children
intro: Pinworms are small, white, thread-like worms that live in the bowel and are among the most common worm infections in children. They are harmless but cause itching around the anus, particularly at night. They spread easily within families, but are simple to treat.

sections.heading: How infection occurs
paragraphs: Adult female worms lay eggs around the anus at night, causing itching. Children scratch and the eggs stick to fingers, nails, bed linen and clothes, and spread to surfaces and toys. Swallowing the eggs after touching the mouth leads to infection, and the cycle continues. Eggs survive for up to two or three weeks on surfaces.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: Itching around the anus or vagina, especially at night, restless sleep, irritability and sometimes redness or small sores from scratching. Some children have no symptoms at all. Occasionally, worms can be seen in the stool or around the anus, looking like tiny white threads about a centimetre long.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Doctors usually diagnose it from the history, or by seeing worms. A tape test in the morning, pressing sticky tape to the skin around the anus, can collect eggs for a laboratory test. Treatment is a tablet or liquid, such as mebendazole, repeated after two weeks. The whole household is usually treated at the same time. Treatment is not usually used in babies without medical advice.

sections.heading: Hygiene measures
paragraphs: Wash hands with soap after the toilet and before meals, keep nails short, avoid nail biting and scratching, shower in the morning, change underwear and bed linen daily on days of treatment, wash at sixty degrees if possible and vacuum bedrooms. Do not share towels.

sections.heading: Reassurance
paragraphs: Pinworms do not mean a child is dirty, and they do not cause serious harm. Children can attend school or nursery once treatment has started. See a doctor if itching persists after treatment, if the child has abdominal pain, or for infections in babies and pregnant women.

examples.title: Doing the hygiene routine
examples.text: Imagine your child has pinworms. You could wash all bedding at high temperature and keep nails short.

examples.title: Treating the family
examples.text: Suppose the doctor prescribes treatment. You might treat everyone in the house on the same day and repeat after two weeks.
